I really don't know where this type of opinion/post should go, so I thought it would be safer to put it in Politics. Sorry if it doesn't fit the bill for you Politics people.

Today, I was listening to a radio show in which the news of Prince's death unfolded in real time. It was The Bennington Show on XM radio. The hosts and following guests said they were shocked, saddened, depressed, it ruined their day, they didn't know what to write, they didn't know what to say, it was a tough day for Minnesota, etc. Upon hearing this, I decided to search for #prince on twitter. A lot of the stuff on that hashtag was much of the same, but some people said they were crying or near crying over their keyboards. Many of them quoted the same poem that happened to have the word "prince" in it.

I don't dispute that Prince was a talented musician or that he was influential. I do dispute the reactions. I assert that most of the reactions, including those of the radio hosts, are simply just virtue signaling. The more saddened you are, the more of an musician or an appreciator of music you are.

To address the "Tough day for Minnesota" aspect. No, it wasn't. Dial 1000 numbers in Minnesota at random and ask the folks how the death of Prince made it a "tough day." Most of them probably didn't know he died. This isn't to say Prince didn't donate to a ton of charities there, or set charities up, or whatever. It's just to say, it wasn't a tough day for Minnesota.

Nor should Prince's death really affect anyone other than people who knew him personally (family, friends, etc). All people die. When my favorite musicians die, which has happened and will happen, my reaction will and always be, "Well, I would have preferred that musician had lived, but stuff happens."

Is there a point to this post? I guess not, other than to express how the reaction to the death of a famous person by me is different than the reaction of others. Cheers.

I agree with your sentiment. I rather like Prince's music. I think he was a bit of a nutbag, but he was extremely talented, and his music has been around for a significant portion of my life.

I might get a little bummed out when I hear about a celebrity death, but we have to face it that none of us make it out alive. I never met a single one of the celebrities whose deaths had what meager impact on my day that they did. Leonard Nimoy probably had the largest impact, because I love Star Trek, and he died of similar health issues as my dad. All in all, I was sad for a bit, and went about my life.

When I found out about Prince, it was a bit...odd...might be the right word. When I found out about David Bowie it felt unreal, like he wasn't actually a person, but instead some completely out there character. His death was kind of a slap in the face of reality that he was indeed actually a human being who could die. Prince was somewhat like that, but nowhere near to the same degree. Then I went back to work. At the end of the day, and every day until it is lost, sold, or destroyed, my copy of Purple Rain is still right there with the rest of my records. Prince's music isn't gone. What have fans, or "fans" actually lost?

It reminds me of my old roommates calling a bunch of their friends asking if they were ok when news of Chris Benoit hit. Why wouldn't they be ok? Did they know Benoit personally? Likely not. Suck it up and move on.

Who is Chris Benoit? I honestly don't know who that is.

When you mentioned David Bowie's death being a bit unreal, that's where I disconnect with the reaction. Unreal? Again, he was very a talented, influential, and versatile character. I loved his acting in The Prestige. He was a good musician and influential on other musicians. Awesome, all of it. But never did I ascribe to him some kind of otherworldly power. He was just a dude. How does that happen for you, where you see another human excelling at something or many somethings and then thinking that person is above/outside humanity?

I think with Bowie, there was just something larger than life about him. It sounds weird, I know. I read comics, so if I saw an article saying "Bruce Wayne dies" I'd be like, what the fuck ever, this is comics, he'll be back in six months. With Bowie it was more of a reaction of "Oh yeah, he wasn't a comic book character". Once again though, nothing really changed in my life. My copy of Labyrinth and my albums are still there. I wouldn't really say "otherworldly", but there was definitely something where I just equated him more to something out of my comic books.

Chris Benoit. My friends reactions were before it was common knowledge about that being a murder. They are huge into wrestling, and did some local circuits at the time.

I was never a fan, but I think some of those are honest reactions. I only say that because when Robin Williams died I shed a little tear. He is the only celebrity death I have ever had a significant reaction too. I loved all of his movies and a lot of them made up a good portion of my childhood. I remember going with my mother to see Aladdin and Hook at the movie theatre, watching Mork and Mindy in reruns, and discovering The World According to Garp (that was before he had made is later stuff).

Anyway, his death was like an official closing of my childhood. I was also pregnant with my first child and remember thinking, "my children are going to grow up in a world where Robin Williams has always been dead, wierd". It saddened me.

Music I think transcends emotion on a much deeper level than movies. Maybe a song helped someone heal, gain courage, or have some self reflection. It's the bond to that piece of art and the appreciation of the person who made it that causes the mourning. A lot of songs Prince produced were deep (When the Doves Cry; Nothing Compares to You). So I can see how fans have that reaction. He also was a major sex icon in the 80's (just imagine if Harry Styles passed away). So a lot of fans just lost their childhood crushes.

So I guess the what you're saying is, people tag certain famous people to their lives, and when that celebrity dies, they feel like some part of their life is lost? That's so strange to me. I remember Aladdin, hell, I LOVED aladdin. I liked a few other of Robin Williams' movies, too. When he died, the only thing I thought was, yep, he did a bunch of coke and it caught up.
